corrections.text: Visits Langholm, Scotland; made a freeman
corrections.reason: Placeholder month was wrong: History UK, Wikipedia (Langholm) and the Purdue Mountbatten-lecture file place the Langholm freedom ceremony in March 1972 (Mountbatten lecture in Edinburgh just before). Moved to 1972-03 as confirmed.

corrections.text: Honorary president of cave expedition in Ecuador
corrections.reason: Expedition ran Jul-Aug 1976 but Armstrong flew in after the cave was de-rigged; Vistazo dates his visit to August 1976 (YRC expedition account agrees he arrived late). Moved to 1976-08 as confirmed.

corrections.text: Gives only press conference at 10th anniversary
corrections.reason: Month of the UC press conference was never found (UC pages give 1979 only). Replaced with the dated White House Rose Garden event of 20 July 1979 (Carter Library photo); the press conference stays unverified.

notes: Second pass: 48 cells, all confirmed (45 new months plus 3 upgrades: 1979-07, 1982-06, 2002-02) and 3 corrections. Merged with the first pass that is 127 confirmed of 608 months (20.9%). The shared WebSearch budget ran out partway, so 1973 (one headline), 1975, 1978-1979 beyond Feb/Jul, 1987, 1990, 1992-1993, 1998, 2001 (Sep only), 2003 stay thin or empty. Evidence types: many cells use Wikimedia Commons file pages that reproduce NASA, US Navy, DVIDS or Carter Library captions with exact photo dates (1964-03, 1965-07, 1965-11, 1966-01, 1969-02, 1969-05, 1970-10, 1979-07, 2005-08, 2007-07, 2008-08, 2008-09, 2009-10, 2010-10, 2011-08, 2012-04); others are opened news, NASA, university, Aviation Week, UPI and House/Senate pages. 1974-03 and 1977-05 come from dated photo captions on the University of Cincinnati library Armstrong site. Weaker items, droppable if only opened-page evidence is wanted: 1964-06 (USGS OF 2005-1190 Table 1 seen in a search snippet: Philmont 3-6 June 1964 with Armstrong listed; page itself returned 403); 1971-06, 1975-12 and 1984-05 (Purdue Armstrong Papers folder titles seen only in snippets; archives.lib.purdue.edu returned 403); 1973-02 (Wikipedia citation: Morning Call headline of 16 Feb 1973); 1983-12 (Wikipedia citation: Esquire, Dec 1983); 1971-12 (Cincinnati Enquirer archive item syndicated on Yahoo, dated 1 Dec 1971); 1976-08 (Vistazo says August 1976; NEXUS gives 3 Aug; Wikipedia says the expedition ran Jul-Aug). Conflicts and judgment calls: 1986-07 is the formal delivery of the National Commission on Space report (SpacePolicyOnline lists Armstrong as a member); NTRS and CSM show a public release in May 1986. 1970-02 uses the Hubbard Medal (Wikipedia cites an AP item of 18 Feb 1970; a dealer lot says 16 Feb); NASA also photographed him at Lewis Research Center that month. 2002-05 rests on Aviation Week (he retires in May) and TWST (Smith elected chairman 7 May 2002); the EDO press release of 8 Feb 2002 (URL pr2002/02r0208) and Aviation Week of 18 Feb 2002 confirm 2002-02, so Wikipedia's citation year 2000 is a typo. 2010-05 also holds the Naval Aviation Hall of Honor induction (14 May 2010, Navy photos); the Senate testimony of 12 May was chosen. 1982-06 text changed from 'Returns to Cincinnati' because UC says he held an adjunct post then; the address was 13 June 1982. Still unconfirmed in the first pass: 1962-03 X-20 (Wikipedia's X-20 page says Armstrong was among seven named in 1960 and left in mid-1962, which sits badly with a 15 Mar 1962 selection), 1979-10 National Aviation Hall of Fame (year only), 2003-02 Columbia memorial. Not used: a NARA photo of Armstrong giving Nixon a plaque (Commons caption says 4 June 1974 but looks unreliable), the Agnew awards of 13/14 Nov 1970 (Armstrong's part not verified), Florida Today headline of 14 Mar 1993 on Gemini astronauts' Hall of Fame events (could not open), Purdue folder titles for speeches in 1978-05, 1991-10, 1993-09, 1999-03 (organisations unclear).
